title: Start order and health
summary: depends_on, healthchecks, and computing a start order with a topological sort.

steps.title: depends_on only orders the start
body: - db           # short form: start db first

The short form only means *"start the db container before the api container"*. Postgres needs a few seconds after its container starts before it accepts connections, so the API can still hit `Connection refused`.
To wait for **readiness**, give the dependency a **healthcheck** and use the long form:
condition: service_healthy     # wait until db's healthcheck passes
Conditions: `service_started` (the default), `service_healthy`, and `service_completed_successfully` (for a one-off job such as a migration that must finish first).

steps.prompt: The API uses the short form `depends_on: [db]` and still fails at startup with `Connection refused`. Why?
options: Short `depends_on` waits only for the db container to start, not for Postgres to accept connections
depends_on only works with `image:` services, not `build:` ones
Compose starts services in alphabetical order, ignoring depends_on
The db service needs `ports:` for the api to reach it
steps.explain: Add a healthcheck to db and `condition: service_healthy` to the API. A retry loop in the app is still wise: databases also restart in production.

steps.prompt: Make the API wait until Postgres reports healthy.
`web` depends on `api`; `api` depends on `db` (condition `service_healthy`). Arrange what Compose does on `docker compose up`.
lines: wait for db's healthcheck to pass
steps.explain: Dependencies first, all the way down; a `service_healthy` condition inserts a wait.

steps.title: Start order is a topological sort
body: Services and their `depends_on` form a **directed graph**. A valid start order lists every service after all of its dependencies: a **topological sort**. One simple way (Kahn's algorithm):
ready = services not yet started whose dependencies have all started
if ready is empty but services remain  →  there is a cycle
start one ready service (here: the alphabetically first, so the order is predictable)
web ──▶ api ──▶ db              order: db, redis, api, web
Compose rejects a cycle (`api` depends on `db`, `db` depends on `api`) with a "dependency cycle detected" error.

steps.explain: First only `db` and `redis` are ready (no dependencies); alphabetical order picks `db`. Then `redis`, then `api` (both its dependencies done), then `web`.

steps.prompt: `api` depends on `worker`, `worker` depends on `api`. What happens on `docker compose up`?
options: Compose refuses to start and reports a dependency cycle
Compose starts both at the same time
Compose starts api, then worker crashes
steps.explain: No order can satisfy both. Usually one of the dependencies is not real: the app can retry instead.

steps.title: Compute the start order
prompt: Write `List<string> StartOrder(Dictionary<string, List<string>> deps)` where `deps[s]` lists the services `s` depends on. Return the services in start order using the algorithm from the card: repeatedly start the alphabetically first (ordinal) service whose dependencies have all started.
If at some point services remain but none is ready, return a single line: `error: dependency cycle among A, B` listing the services that could not start, sorted.
solution: return new List<string> { "error: dependency cycle among " + string.Join(", ", stuck) };
template: Dojo.Eq("web, api, db, redis", new List<string> { "db", "redis", "api", "web" }, StartOrder(new Dictionary<string, List<string>> { ["web"] = new() { "api" }, ["api"] = new() { "db", "redis" }, ["db"] = new(), ["redis"] = new() }));
Dojo.Eq("independent services are alphabetical", new List<string> { "a", "b", "c" }, StartOrder(new Dictionary<string, List<string>> { ["c"] = new(), ["a"] = new(), ["b"] = new() }));

Dojo.Eq("migration before api", new List<string> { "db", "migrate", "api", "worker" }, StartOrder(new Dictionary<string, List<string>> { ["api"] = new() { "migrate" }, ["worker"] = new() { "api", "db" }, ["migrate"] = new() { "db" }, ["db"] = new() }));

Dojo.Eq("cycle", new List<string> { "error: dependency cycle among api, web, worker" }, StartOrder(new Dictionary<string, List<string>> { ["db"] = new(), ["api"] = new() { "worker" }, ["worker"] = new() { "api" }, ["web"] = new() { "api" } }));
hints: If no service is ready, everything not yet started is stuck.

steps.title: Start order from compose.yaml
prompt: Now read it from the file. Write `string ComposeOrder(List<string> lines)` returning `start order: A, B, C` (or the cycle error line from the last exercise).
`depends_on` comes in two forms; support both:
depends_on:          # short form: list items at indent 6
depends_on:          # long form: names at indent 6, ending in ':'
condition: service_healthy     # indent 8, ignore it here

**The YAML subset** (all tests use it): two spaces per indent level, no tabs. `services:` sits at column 0; each service name is at indent 2 (`api:`); its keys are at indent 4 (`image: x`, or `ports:` with nothing after the colon); list items are at indent 6 (`- "8080:8080"`). Strip surrounding `"` or `'` from values and items. Ignore blank lines, `#` comments and every other top-level key (`volumes:`, `networks:`) and what is under it.
solution: if (indent == 2) { svc = line.TrimEnd(':'); deps[svc] = new List<string>(); }
string? next = deps.Keys.Where(s => !done.Contains(s) && deps[s].All(done.Contains)).OrderBy(s => s, StringComparer.Ordinal).FirstOrDefault();
return "error: dependency cycle among " + string.Join(", ", deps.Keys.Where(s => !done.Contains(s)).OrderBy(s => s, StringComparer.Ordinal));
template: Dojo.Eq("full stack", "start order: db, redis, api, web", ComposeOrder(dojoStack));
Dojo.Eq("no dependencies", "start order: a, b", ComposeOrder(new List<string> { "services:", "  b:", "    image: x", "  a:", "    image: y" }));
Dojo.Eq("cycle", "error: dependency cycle among a, b", ComposeOrder(new List<string> { "services:", "  a:", "    depends_on:", "      - b", "  b:", "    depends_on:", "      - a" }));
hints: Remember the current indent-4 key, so you only collect indent-6 lines under `depends_on`.
A healthcheck's `test:` line is also at indent 6: that is why you must check the key.
Reuse your `StartOrder` loop once the dictionary is built.
